g.text: Operands push directly | Operators pop & evaluate while prec(top) ≥ prec(incoming)
→ operator stack was empty, so '+' pushed directly: [+]
No evaluation yet: only one operator exists, waiting for next token.
Since incoming '*' has strictly higher priority than top '+', NO pop occurs!
Rule: A higher priority operator waits on top to be resolved first.
See '/': equal priority to top '*' triggers POP & EVAL, then push 8
Push result 24 to operand stack. Operand is now: [2, 24]
Compare '/' with new top '+': prec('/')=2 > prec('+')=1 → Push '/'
Left-to-right evaluation preserved: '*' evaluated before '/' could be pushed!
See '-': Cascading pop of '/' then '+' (two successive reductions)
Push 3 to operand stack. Operand stack is now: [2, 3]
Compare '-' with new top '+': prec('-')=1 == prec('+')=1 → POP + too!
Push 5 to operand stack. Operand stack is now: [5]
Operator stack now empty → push '-' directly: [-]
End of String: Flush Remaining Operator & Finalize Result
String ended. Flush remaining operator stack while ostack.size() > 0:
Push 2 to operand stack. Operator stack is now empty!
while (ostack.size() > 0 && ostack.peek() != '(' && precedence(ostack.peek()) >= precedence(ch)) { pop op, v2, v1; push operation(v1, v2, op); } ostack.push(ch);
